newsitem.title: SPAIN: Dealers still suspect BoS is buying mark/peseta.
newsitem.headline: Dealers still suspect BoS is buying mark/peseta.

text.p: The Bank of Spain is probably still buying marks for pesetas in an attempt to stem the appreciation of the Spanish unit, forex traders said on Friday.

The central bank was likely operating discreetly via several entities, which would explain the peseta's difficulty in staying under 84.10 to the mark despite continued strong gains in bonos, they said.
As usual, the Bank of Spain itself declined to comment.
"We think the Bank of Spain is buying marks at around 84.09 to the mark," said one dealer, adding that this is just where the peseta's rise was continually stemmed.
At 1030 GMT the December bond future was trading at 107.06, up 79 basis points from yesterday's close. The 10-year bono-Bund yield spread was at 177 basis points, down from 190 at Thursday's close.
